# Preface {.unnumbered}

As outlined in the  [Introduction](https://firstepoch.github.io/handbook/intro.html), we made this handbook out of a belief that AI research is unusual: the barrier to entry is relatively low in terms of resources and formal requirements, yet the path to mentorship is rather difficult. We believe the field benefits from a diverse pool of researchers of all ages and from the cultivation of good scientific practices, and our hope is that this handbook makes the path to mentorship a little easier.

## About this handbook

This handbook is a collection of resources to help you break into AI research, expand your breadth, and cultivate good scientific practices. Formed by our own experiences of starting in this field at high school, the handbook is aimed primarily at junior researchers, hence the name. One of the primary guiding principle we've applied while making it is this: we aim to answer the questions we had while working on our own first AI projects and papers, when we didn't have anyone to turn to. We should note, though, that even as we joined labs and continued our research paths in more formal settings, we have found that many things are left unsaid. The gaps this handbook aims to fill are hence even for folks already working at labs, in graduate programs, and more.

## Overview

We are upfront in that this is not an AI textbook. We do not aim to duplicate many excellent resources that already cover fundamental math, algorithms, and architectures needed for work in this field. Rather, we aim to fill gaps between these resources, and organize them into a bigger picture. That said, we do not aim to merely catalogue or theorize; this handbook offers a rather practical framing. Beyond leaving motivated, we hope to equip you with a bigger picture of research in the field, and intuition around core concepts that will be applicable across problems and data.

## Authorship

All prose in this handbook was written and edited by us, Alice Hemain and Maty Bohacek, with the exception of grammar checking performed by AI and other software tools.

AI has been used to help with the maintenance of this web app, the creation of plots, as well as other coding tasks, as indicated in the git history. The project is open to external contributions subject to our Contribution policies, which, among others, restrict the use of AI writing.
